title: BlackTech_PLEAD_Backdoor_Investigation_b16
description: Investigate and respond to a potential BlackTech PLEAD backdoor malware incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity potentially related to the BlackTech threat group. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host. Use the provided credentials to access the target host and enter 'start' to begin the investigation and progress to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the provided credentials to access the target host and enter 'start' to begin the investigation and progress to the next level.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Connections
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you've noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate these connections to determine if they're malicious. Submit the suspicious port number.
levels.solution: Check active network connections and listen ports on the target host. The suspicious port is 4444 used for command and control communication.

hints.title: First hint
hints.content: Start by examining active network connections on the target host.

hints.title: Second hint
hints.content: Look for unusual or unexpected ports that are listening or actively connected.

hints.title: Third hint
hints.content: Use the 'ss' command to check active network connections and listening ports.

levels.title: Analyze Suspicious Service
levels.content: You've discovered a suspicious service running on the target host. Analyze this service to understand its behavior and determine if it's related to the BlackTech threat group. Submit the service configuration file path.
levels.solution: Examine the service configuration and logs to understand its purpose and behavior. The service name is bkd.service and its associated configuration files are located in /etc/systemd/system/bkd.service.

hints.title: First hint
hints.content: Begin by checking the status of the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint
hints.content: Look for service configuration files in typical locations such as /etc/systemd/system/

hints.title: Third hint
hints.content: Use the 'systemctl status' command followed by the service name to gather more information.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Evidence suggests that the attacker may have moved laterally from the target host to another system. Investigate this possibility and determine if sensitive data has been exfiltrated. Submit the service name responsible for lateral movement.
levels.solution: Check for file transfers and remote execution commands involving other hosts in the network. The service responsible for lateral movement is payload-transfer.service and the destination host is next-target.

hints.title: First hint
hints.content: Start by examining services that might be responsible for lateral movement.

hints.title: Second hint
hints.content: Look for services that involve file transfers or remote execution commands.

hints.title: Third hint
hints.content: Use the 'systemctl status' command followed by the service name to gather more information.
